summary: Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Martin King Whyte, having also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned a bachelor's degree at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and a PhD at Harvard University (~1993–2000), later becoming Associate Professor at UC Irvine (~2007).

Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) was a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from INALCO. He served at the University of California as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies (~1985–2004) and Professor Emeritus at UCSB.

Allan Gibbard (born 1942) is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (B.A. ~1959–1963) and Harvard University (Ph.D. ~1965–1971). He held appointments at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. In 1981, he joined Pomona College as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures.

Allan Harrison Fry (1910–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton (A.B. ~1928–1932), Basel, and Bonn (1935–1937). He taught at Fordham, The New School, and the Catholic University of America (Assistant Professor, 1941).

Allen Wright Thrasher (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1967–1974), studied with traditional Indian scholars, and worked at the Library of Congress (~1984–2013).
Allison Busch (1969–2020) was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She served as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer (1853–1930) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a Ph.D. at Würzburg (1874–1879) under Julius Jolly and studied with Georg Bühler. He held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1885–1898) and Lucknow Museum (1884–1899).

Alois Closs (1893–1984) researched religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After degrees at the University of Graz, he taught at Akademisches Gymnasium Graz (1921–1941), studied in Vienna (1933–1936), and served as librarian at Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek (1941–1958).

Alois Müller (1835–1901) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held positions at Vienna University Library (~1867–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and Graz University Library as Director (1879).

Alois Vaníček (1825–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1843–1847) under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. In 1882, he became Professor of Comparative Literature and Sanskrit at Charles University.

Alois Walde (1869–1924) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Innsbruck under Friedrich Stolz and studied at Leipzig. He was Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Giessen (1909–1912), Innsbruck (1912), and Königsberg (1922–1924).

Aloysius Pieris (1934–2026) studied Buddhist philosophy and theology, earning degrees from London, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre (1974) and held visiting chairs at Washington Theological Union, Vanderbilt, and Union Theological Seminary.

Alphonse François Lacroix (1799–1859) was active in linguistics and religious studies. He worked with the Netherlands Missionary Society (1821) and the London Missionary Society (1825), and founded the Bhowanipore Missionary Institution in 1851.
Alubomulle Sumanasara (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1980 to 1986 under the supervision of Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë (born 1964) is a philosopher who studied at Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard (~1988–1995). He held faculty posts at CUNY (~1995–1996), UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), and UC Berkeley (from ~2003).

Alvan Clark Eastman (1894–1959) worked in Indology and art history, studying at Harvard and NYU. He held curatorial roles at the Detroit Institute of Arts (1925–1929) and served as director of museums in Evansville, Pasadena, and Winnipeg.

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religion, earning doctorates at Ceylon and Oxford. He served as professor at Peradeniya, Jaffna, and Uppsala, and was Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (2002–2009).
